html:
The Varangians were Norsemen, mostly from what is now eastern Sweden, who travelled east across the Baltic and down the rivers of Russia and Ukraine in the 800s to 1000s, as traders, raiders and soldiers.

They followed the Volga and the Dnieper to the Caspian and the Black Sea, trading furs and slaves for silver. By tradition a Varangian named Rurik took power at Novgorod in 862, and his family ruled Kievan Rus', whose name may come from a Finnish word for Swedes. Within a few generations they became Slavic in speech.

Others served the Byzantine emperor in the Varangian Guard. Runestones in Sweden name men who died in the east or in Greece. Their routes linked Scandinavia to Baghdad and Constantinople, through markets like Birka. See Sweden.
